newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Rebels join Sierra Leone coup leaders - military.
newsitem.headline: Rebels join Sierra Leone coup leaders - military.

text.p: Rebel commanders have joined leaders of a coup in Sierra Leone and are rejecting any mediation to try and reverse the overthrow of the elected government, military and diplomatic sources said on Friday.
They said leaders of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF) waging a guerrilla campaign since 1991 but now welcomed as allies by the coupmakers, entered the capital two days ago.

"The RUF leaders came out of the bush and entered the town. Now it seems the soldiers have got more than they bargained for because the rebels are now calling the shots," a West African peacekeeping officer said.

A diplomat involved with attempts to strike a deal with coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah said a veteran politician sent to mediation talks at military headquarters on Thursday night found 50 rebel commanders there.
"They were sitting with the coup leaders, who had their military ranks stripped from their uniforms," the diplomat said, quoting the politician.
"It is a serious problem because the rebels have rejeced any mediation. They say they are ready to fight to the end and are prepared for anything," he said.
Uncertainty heightened in the capital on Friday as United States marines airlifted frightened Americans and other foreigners fleeing violence, pillaging and rape that followed Sunday's coup.

Regional power Nigeria has built up a military force in Freetown in preparation for a strike against the coup soldiers to try and enfore a regional order for the restoration of the toppled elected government.

In what looked like the last major evacuation of Westerners, 15 U.S. navy helicopters shuttled about 600 foreigners, including just over 300 Americans, to the helicopter-carrier Kearsarge lying offshore.
